**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

The agreement imposes no audit, inspection or usage-verification right on the Client, so we sit better than the playbook's preferred position — there is no frequency, notice, cost-allocation or system-access term that needs constraining. I did not treat this as a "missing" clause because the rule is protective of the customer; drafting in audit machinery would manufacture an obligation against us.

One point to carry forward in negotiation (noted in the rationale, not flagged): the absence of an express clause means there are also no guardrails if TrueLink later asks to verify usage. If the Vendor proposes audit language, we should hold to the preferred limits — once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor bound by confidentiality, Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and no direct access to our systems.
